header:
Date: 2025-04-02
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Brooks (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Helix AI - Head of MLOps), Priya Anand (Helix AI - VP Eng), Sam Torres (Helix AI - CTO), Lina Gomez (Helix - Platform Eng)
summary: Quarterly health check covering steady growth in tokens, a billing spike in March attributed to an opt-in batch job, discussion of latency SLOs and two recent incidents, and follow-up on reserved capacity pricing and P95 benchmark testing.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is the QBR / health check for Helix AI. we have about 55 minutes, we've got Jordan, Priya, Sam, Lina from Helix and Ethan and I from Redwood. quick agenda: usage, cost, reliability, roadmap, then next steps.

[00:24] Jordan: Thanks Maya. yeah we saw steady growth month over month, tokens up ~28% qtr over qtr. the big ask today is: cost control and making sure latency doesn't regress as we scale.

[00:38] Ethan: quick context from our side - we've been watching your per-route P95 and the Redwood Console shows a slight uptick in late March. looks correlated with a nightly batch rerank job that spilled into peak hours.

[01:05] Priya: right, that batch job was an experiment that we forgot to cap, so it ran during business hours. billing spiked by about 42% that week. any recommendations?

[01:22] Maya: yeah so two levers: move heavy batch to off-peak or use a dedicated pool for the batch. Reserved capacity can be cheaper per-token for steady usage, and Dedicated burst can isolate those runs. I'll share pricing.

[01:41] Sam: how big is the delta between hosted and reserved capacity? like what sort of commit do we need to see benefits?

[01:53] Maya: typical math — if you have predictable baseline throughput, a monthly commit gets you a ~20-35% reduction on unit cost depending on model and quantization. we'll send modeled scenarios.

[02:10] Lina: related — we care about data isolation, logs, and audit for SOC2 right now. is there any lift to move to Dedicated or Private?

[02:22] Ethan: Dedicated gives tenant isolation and consistent throughput. Private (VPC/on-prem) is more for regulated environments and needs a bit more infra work. for SOC2 you can stay hosted but enable SSO, KMS, audit logs — we have a security packet we'll share.

[02:45] Jordan: we had two incidents in March — one 20-min outage due to a model variant rollout and one performance regression at P95. can you walk us through root cause?

[03:02] Ethan: sure. the outage happened during a canary rollout; the autoscaler mis-specified a GPU type mismatch in the deployment descriptor, which caused a fallback and a transient overload. the regressed P95 was the batch spillover I mentioned. we've put a guardrail in the rollout pipeline to catch GPU-type mismatches and tightened the autoscaler thresholds.

[03:34] Priya: is there anything we should change in our runbooks?

[03:41] Maya: yes, add an explicit pre-rollout check for model variant compat with instance types, and schedule heavy re-ranking outside business hours or pin it to a dedicated pool. also, set up an alert for token-rate deviation in Console so you see the batch starting.

[04:05] Jordan: send over a doc for the pre-rollout checklist and the alert playbook.

[04:12] Maya: will do. link to the playbook (internal): https://redwood.ai/docs/runbooks/helix-pre-rollout (sent in chat).

[04:28] Lina: on observability — the Console shows token-level cost but it's a bit noisy. any tips to slice by route and model?

[04:38] Ethan: you can create per-route dashboards and set a cost attribution tag. also Enable continuous evals on a small prompt set so you can detect quality regressions after rollouts.

[04:54] Sam: what's the expected latency if we move to quantized model and dedicated GPU pool?

[05:02] Ethan: typically quantization + optimized kernels reduces P50 by 10-20% and P95 by around 5-15%, depends on prompt length. for your workloads (avg seq len ~420 tokens) we estimate P95 goes from ~480ms to ~360ms on the dedicated pool with Q4 quantization profile. we'll bench and share numbers.

[05:30] Priya: any gotchas on quantization? quality loss?

[05:36] Ethan: small regression risk — we recommend running quality evals against your 200 example prompts. Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles and flag regressions.

[05:50] Jordan: about billing — we want a breakdown for March with the batch spike separated.

[05:57] Maya: we'll pull a billing export and highlight the anomalous routes. I'll attach the sheet. link: https://redwood.ai/finance/exports/helix-march-billing.csv (placeholder link).

[06:12] Priya: also curious on retention: logs and usage — do you have a retention tiering?

[06:20] Ethan: yes, audit logs are configurable; you can change retention per project. longer retention may have additional cost.

[06:30] Sam: one strategic question — we're considering building a partial on-prem inference mesh for latency-critical customers. is that something Redwood supports?

[06:40] Maya: yes, Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem packages. there's an integration path but it takes more ops time. often customers start with Dedicated and then evaluate Private for compliance/latency needs.

[07:00] Jordan: what's the timeline if we wanted to pilot Dedicated in Q2?

[07:07] Maya: we can provision a dedicated pool in ~2 weeks after sign off; benchmarks + POC are typically 1-2 weeks. so it fits a Q2 pilot.

[07:18] Ethan: for the POC we'll need sample prompts, a representative traffic profile, and target SLOs.

[07:28] Jordan: we'll share those.

[07:35] Priya: any regression alerts already in place? we saw one false positive last month.

[07:42] Ethan: that's likely from broad eval thresholds. we'll tweak thresholds and enable per-deployment rollup metrics to reduce noise.

[07:55] Lina: security review — one ask from our auditors: can you confirm key rotation cadence and KMS integrations?

[08:05] Maya: yes, we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and can document rotation cadence in the security packet. I'll ask our security reviewer to send the SOC2 artifacts.

[08:18] Jordan: great.

[08:22] Maya: quick note on model routing — if you want cheaper fallbacks during peak, we can route lower-cost quantized variants for non-critical routes. that's an automated fallback policy we can configure.

[08:36] Sam: interesting. that could cut costs without impacting core flows.

[08:44] Ethan: also, prefix/KV caching can reduce token replay for, say, system-level prompts. we saw ~12% token savings on similar customers.

[09:00] Priya: is that hard to implement?

[09:05] Ethan: it's a runtime config; we need examples of common prefixes and we'll recommend TTLs.

[09:15] Jordan: what's the risk of using caching with context changes?

[09:20] Ethan: main risk is stale prefix state; we recommend short TTLs for dynamic contexts and test coverage in your evals.

[09:33] Priya: any ask from you folks to us?

[09:38] Maya: share prompt set and traffic profile, confirm whether you want a reserved capacity proposal, and confirm SOC2 doc recipients.

[09:50] Jordan: will do.

[09:55] Maya: ok let's recap next steps — Maya will send pricing + billing export annotated; Ethan will run the P95 bench and share the recording; Helix will provide prompts and SLOs.

[10:10] Priya: thanks everyone. one last question — can you send the demo recording?

[10:16] Maya: yes recording and the deck (link): https://redwood.ai/decks/qbr-helix-apr2025.pdf (sent).

[10:24] Sam: thanks, that's helpful.

[10:28] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up on the action items.

[10:33] [meeting ends]

Notes: transcript contains occasional transcription artifacts ("K-V cac" instead of KV cache), speaker overlap, and some mis-attributed labels typical of automated capture. Shared artifacts: QBR deck, billing CSV, runbook link.
